findings.reason: the node must also widen the observer release path (or the section must say that landed/dropped leave the observer hold only for a peer-caused row), and as written its gate would fail or the worker would widen the filter blindly.
findings.text: §14 says landed and dropped rows "are now carried once each", blaming the observer class from `transition_class`, but the effective suppression for the sequence in its own done-when is `_observer_exception` at `reckon/crew/ticker.py:1499-1512`: it returns False for a run that has already been "told" (delivery printed, `_told` set at `ticker.py:1482`) whose destination is a settled state (`promoted`, `recorded`, `withdrawn`, `discarded`), and `_feed` drops that row without appending it, so `stream_carries` never sees it; adding landed/dropped to the carried rule alone therefore leaves the implement run's "then promoted" row unprinted and the done-when unachievable

findings.reason: the two clauses cannot both hold until the plan names the fact that distinguishes a coordinator-caused landing from a peer's, so a node must either violate one clause or invent an event field the plan does not specify.
findings.text: §14 requires landed rows "carried once each" while also keeping "a row the coordinator's own merge or discard caused … withheld only where the coordinator's own command already printed the outcome", but the transition event built by `recovery_watch._watch_transition` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1853-1905) carries no cause or actor field, and the only memory distinguishing the cases is `_told`, which suppresses every post-delivery landing including a peer's

findings.reason: the node can implement dropped rows wrongly or omit them entirely and still pass its gate, so a shipped defect in half the section's declared scope goes unmeasured.
findings.text: the done-when sequence is "dispatched, starting, working, delivered, the review's dispatched, starting and working, the review's delivered, then promoted" and expects a landing row, but never feeds a moved-away run (a `withdrawn` or `discarded` transition) even though §14 carries "landed and dropped" as two equally weighted new kinds; the dropped half of the declaration has no arm, and the negative control names only the launch and in-review row

findings.reason: the followup body is the plan's dispatch driver, so a coordinator following it would launch §5 and §7 directly after §4, concurrently with §14 on the same file, instead of sequencing §14 first.
findings.text: §14 newly declares "§5 and §7 run after §14, which writes `ticker.py` before them", but §5:227 still says "It runs after §4, which writes `ticker.py`", and the followup driver at :335 still reads "§3 follows §2, and §5 then §7 follow §4" with §14 unnamed; §14 is now a second writer of `ticker.py` standing between §4 and §5
